knitr::opts_chunk$set(

## Introduction

The shinyfilters hex sticker is intentionally simple, modelled after classic R 
package hex stickers. The package name is readable and centered at the bottom, 
and features an icon above it.

```{=html}
<div style="display: flex; gap: 10px;">
  <div style="flex: 50%;">
		<img src="figures/datatable.png" id="hex-datatable" alt="data.table package hex sticker, a walrus at the center, with the word 'data.table' centered on the bottom.">
  </div>
  <div style="flex: 50%;">
		<img src="figures/bookdown.png" id="hex-bookdown" alt="bookdown package hex sticker, which features an icon of a quill put to a book. Beneath the icon is the work bookdown, centered.">
  </div>
</div>
```
<br>

For the icon, I wanted to pay respects to shiny, while distinguishing this 
package as an extension, rather than a core shiny package.

Looking at Posit's hex stickers you can see this pattern. Compare {shinytest2}
with {shinychat}.

```{=html}
<div style="display: flex; gap: 10px;">
  <div style="flex: 50%;">
		<img src="figures/shinytest2.svg" id="hex-shinytest2" alt="shinytest2 package hex sticker, which resembles the shiny hex sticker.">
  </div>
  <div style="flex: 50%;">
		<img src="figures/shinychat.svg" id="hex-shinychat" alt="shinychat package hex sticker, which resembles a classic hex sticker: Icon on top, text centered on bottom.">
  </div>
</div>
```
<br>

So we take the swoosh from Shiny, and work it in with our minimalist filter 
icon:

```{=html}
<div style="display: flex; gap: 10px;">
  <div style="flex: 50%;">
		<img src="figures/shiny.svg" id="hex-shiny" alt="shiny package hex sticker, a blue background with shiny centered in a scripted font, featuring a pominent swoosh originating from the y, underlining the word.">
  </div>
  <div style="flex: 50%;">
		<img src="../logo.svg" id="hex-shinyfilters" alt="shinyfilters package hex sticker, which features the shiny swoosh but is emblematic of a classic hex sticker: swoosh + funnel icon on top. shinyfilters in plain text centered on bottom."">
  </div>
</div>
```
<br>

For the icon, despite being minimal, I had a few objectives in mind:

### The swoosh

* The swoosh must be the actual swoosh from the shiny hex sticker.
* The circle implied by the left end of the swoosh must be the same width as
  as the top of the funnel.
* Where the bottom of the funnel's circle and the swoosh meet, they must 
  coincide.
* The circle implied by the right end of the swoosh must coincide with the top 
  right of the funnel

### The color

* The filter icon color must resemble `cli::col_magenta()`
* The background must be a complentary purple, dark enough to meet >= 3.1 
  contrast ratio

With these guidelines (and about 30 drafts) Opus 5.5 was able to build and 
validate the design.

What follows is the ~1400 lines of R code used to draw the logo.

## Load packages
The outlines of the letters are read with systemfonts and textshaping.
```{r}
library(systemfonts)
library(textshaping)
```

## Sources

There are two sources for the logo, the shiny hex sticker and the font.

```{r}
shiny_url <- paste0(
	"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rstudio/hex-stickers/",
	"69528093ef59f541e5a4798dbcb00e60267e8870/SVG/shiny.svg"
)
font_url <- paste0(
	"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/fonts/",
	"00ab40e1cdf29190ad0c1432c079f950185e11f4/",
	"ofl/baloo2/Baloo2-Medium.ttf"
)
```

## Configuration

### Colors

```{r}
# originally was a gradient from #4A0D82 to #1C0038, but graident was later
# removed
sky <- c("#4A0D82", "#4A0D82") # the sticker, top to bottom
edge <- "#10002B" # its border
ink <- "#FFFFFF" # the word and the swoosh
```

The funnel has no colors here: they are worked out from the sticker's,
[below](#the-colors-of-the-funnel). It stands out from the sticker by this
much, as WCAG measures contrast, which is a little more than the 3 that it asks
for.

```{r}
contrast <- 3.1
```

### Sticker dimensions

Everything below is in the sticker's units unless it says otherwise: 2521 wide
and 2911 high, with y running down. The Shiny sticker is the same size.

```{r}
size <- c(2521, 2911)
edge_width <- 72 # of the border
margin <- edge_width # between the border and what is nearest to it
```

### Package name

How big the word is and where it sits are not set here: the swoosh and the
border decide them, [below](#where-things-sit).

```{r}
word <- "shinyfilters"
```

### Swoosh adjustments

Shiny's swoosh is drawn against the baseline of Shiny's lettering, which climbs
at `level`. `foot` is a point on that baseline, on Shiny's sticker: the foot of
the "h". The swoosh is first put in units in which `foot` is at 0 and the
baseline is level, with x along it and y down from it.

```{r}
level <- 7.5
foot <- c(760, 1548)
```

There it is stretched along and across the baseline, about the point
`swoosh_cut`, which is on the stroke that joined its head to the "y". Then it
is scaled, and turned to climb again: at `climb`, which is the angle it climbs
at in Shiny's logo, and by `swoosh_tilt` more, where less than 0 is steeper.
`swoosh_cut` then goes at `swoosh_at` on the sticker. That is not yet where the
swoosh ends up: it and the funnel are moved together,
[below](#where-things-sit), to their place by the border.

```{r}
swoosh_cut <- c(1463, -73)
swoosh_stretch <- c(1.95, 1.3)
swoosh_scale <- 0.462
climb <- 7.5
swoosh_tilt <- -2.8
swoosh_at <- c(2113, 1197)
swoosh_run <- 40 # how far round its circle the head runs on, in degrees
```

### Funnel size

Where it is, how wide its mouth is, how high its lip is, where its cone ends
and its spout starts, and how long its spout is are not set here: the swoosh
and the word decide them, [below](#the-funnel).

```{r}
funnel_spout <- 150 # half-width of the spout
funnel_cut <- 160 # the spout is cut at a slant: its left ends this much higher
funnel_round <- 90 # width of the line drawn round it, which rounds its corners
```

## Download sources

The shiny svg and the source font are downloaded; the Shiny sticker is read as 
one string.

```{r}
shiny_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".svg")
font_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".ttf")
download.file(shiny_url, shiny_file, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
download.file(font_url, font_file, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)

shiny_svg <- paste(readLines(shiny_file, warn = FALSE), collapse = " ")
```

## Helper functions

### Path parsing

```{r}
# Path data of the one path in the Shiny sticker with this class
shiny_path <- function(class) {
	pattern <- sprintf('<path class="%s" d="([^"]*)"', class)
	path <- regmatches(shiny_svg, regexec(pattern, shiny_svg))[[1]][2]
	gsub("\\s+", " ", path)
}

# Splits path data into subpaths. Each is a data frame of absolute segments,
# one per row: start (x0, y0), control points, end (x, y). Lines are stored
# as curves whose control points sit on their ends.
parse_path <- function(data) {
	token <- "[MmLlHhVvCcSsZz]|-?[0-9]*\\.?[0-9]+"
	tokens <- regmatches(data, gregexpr(token, data))[[1]]
	subpaths <- list()
	segments <- list()
	at <- c(0, 0)
	start <- at
	smooth <- NULL
	command <- ""
	i <- 1

	take <- function(n) {
		values <- as.numeric(tokens[i:(i + n - 1)])
		i <<- i + n
		values
	}
	segment <- function(c1, c2, to) {
		row <- data.frame(
			x0 = at[1],
			y0 = at[2],
			x1 = c1[1],
			y1 = c1[2],
			x2 = c2[1],
			y2 = c2[2],
			x = to[1],
			y = to[2]
		)
		segments[[length(segments) + 1]] <<- row
		at <<- to
	}
	finish <- function() {
		if (length(segments) > 0) {
			subpaths[[length(subpaths) + 1]] <<- do.call(rbind, segments)
		}
		segments <<- list()
	}

	while (i <= length(tokens)) {
		if (grepl("[A-Za-z]", tokens[i])) {
			command <- tokens[i]
			i <- i + 1
		}
		origin <- if (command == tolower(command)) at else c(0, 0)
		type <- toupper(command)
		if (type == "M") {
			finish()
			at <- take(2) + origin
			start <- at
			command <- if (command == "m") "l" else "L"
		} else if (type == "L") {
			to <- take(2) + origin
			segment(at, to, to)
		} else if (type == "H") {
			to <- c(take(1) + origin[1], at[2])
			segment(at, to, to)
		} else if (type == "V") {
			to <- c(at[1], take(1) + origin[2])
			segment(at, to, to)
		} else if (type == "C") {
			values <- take(6)
			smooth <- values[3:4] + origin
			segment(values[1:2] + origin, smooth, values[5:6] + origin)
		} else if (type == "S") {
			values <- take(4)
			c1 <- if (is.null(smooth)) at else 2 * at - smooth
			smooth <- values[1:2] + origin
			segment(c1, smooth, values[3:4] + origin)
		} else if (type == "Z") {
			at <- start
			finish()
		}
		if (!type %in% c("C", "S")) {
			smooth <- NULL
		}
	}
	finish()
	subpaths
}

# Moves segments from Shiny's sticker into the units in which `foot` is at 0
# and the baseline of Shiny's lettering is level
leveled <- function(segments) {
	angle <- level * pi / 180
	for (point in list(
		c("x0", "y0"),
		c("x1", "y1"),
		c("x2", "y2"),
		c("x", "y")
	)) {
		x <- segments[[point[1]]] - foot[1]
		y <- segments[[point[2]]] - foot[2]
		segments[[point[1]]] <- x * cos(angle) - y * sin(angle)
		segments[[point[2]]] <- x * sin(angle) + y * cos(angle)
	}
	segments
}
```

### Curves and circles

```{r}
# Handles of a segment, one in each row
handles <- function(segment) {
	matrix(unlist(segment[c("x0", "x1", "x2", "x", "y0", "y1", "y2", "y")]), 4)
}

# Points along a curve with these handles
bezier <- function(handles, t = seq(0, 1, length.out = 60)) {
	cbind((1 - t)^3, 3 * (1 - t)^2 * t, 3 * (1 - t) * t^2, t^3) %*% handles
}

# The circle that a curve with these handles is curving along where it
# starts: its middle and its radius
circle_at_start <- function(handles) {
	speed <- 3 * (handles[2, ] - handles[1, ])
	bend <- 6 * (handles[1, ] - 2 * handles[2, ] + handles[3, ])
	curvature <- (speed[1] * bend[2] - speed[2] * bend[1]) / sum(speed^2)^1.5
	list(
		middle = handles[1, ] +
			c(-speed[2], speed[1]) / sqrt(sum(speed^2)) / curvature,
		radius = abs(1 / curvature)
	)
}

# The circle that lies nearest to points, one in each row, and how far off
# it each point is
circle_through <- function(points) {
	off <- function(circle) {
		sqrt((points[, 1] - circle[1])^2 + (points[, 2] - circle[2])^2) - circle[3]
	}
	# The nearest by the squares of the distances, which can be solved for,
	# is where the search starts
	first <- qr.solve(cbind(2 * points, 1), rowSums(points^2))
	first[3] <- sqrt(first[3] + sum(first[1:2]^2))
	fit <- optim(
		first,
		function(circle) sum(off(circle)^2),
		method = "BFGS",
		control = list(reltol = 1e-15, maxit = 1000)
	)
	list(middle = fit$par[1:2], radius = fit$par[3], off = off(fit$par))
}
```

### Letters

```{r}
# Outlines of the letters of a string, 1000 units to the em with y = 0 on
# the baseline, one row for each point
outlines <- function(text) {
	glyphs <- shape_text(text, path = font_file, size = 1000, res = 72)$shape
	letters <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(glyphs)), function(i) {
		outline <- glyph_outline(
			glyphs$index[i],
			path = font_file,
			size = 1000,
			tolerance = 0.2
		)
		data.frame(
			letter = i,
			contour = paste(i, outline$contour),
			x = outline$x + glyphs$x_offset[i],
			y = glyphs$y_offset[1] - glyphs$y_offset[i] - outline$y,
			stringsAsFactors = FALSE
		)
	})
	do.call(rbind, letters)
}
```

### Shapes on the sticker

```{r}
# Path data for closed shapes, each a matrix of points
path_data <- function(shapes) {
	paths <- vapply(
		shapes,
		function(shape) {
			points <- sprintf("%.1f,%.1f", shape[, 1], shape[, 2])
			paste0("M", paste(points, collapse = "L"), "Z")
		},
		""
	)
	paste(paths, collapse = "")
}

# Points turned through an angle, as SVG's rotate() turns them
turned <- function(points, angle) {
	angle <- angle * pi / 180
	cbind(
		points[, 1] * cos(angle) - points[, 2] * sin(angle),
		points[, 1] * sin(angle) + points[, 2] * cos(angle)
	)
}

# Where the hands of a clock point, this far from `middle`
on_clock <- function(hours, radius, middle = size / 2) {
	turn <- hours * pi / 6
	cbind(middle[1] + radius * sin(turn), middle[2] - radius * cos(turn))
}

# A vector made 1 long
unit <- function(v) {
	v / sqrt(sum(v^2))
}

# Points as SVG lists the corners of a polygon
points <- function(x, y) {
	paste(sprintf("%.1f,%.1f", x, y), collapse = " ")
}

# A hexagon this far inside the edge of the sticker
hexagon <- function(inset) {
	corners <- on_clock(seq(0, 10, by = 2), (size[1] / 2 - inset) / cos(pi / 6))
	points(corners[, 1], corners[, 2])
}

# A gradient through these colors, between two points on the sticker
gradient <- function(id, colors, from, to) {
	c(
		sprintf('<linearGradient id="%s" gradientUnits="userSpaceOnUse"', id),
		sprintf(
			' x1="%.1f" y1="%.1f" x2="%.1f" y2="%.1f">',
			from[1],
			from[2],
			to[1],
			to[2]
		),
		sprintf(
			'<stop offset="%s" stop-color="%s"/>',
			seq(0, 1, length.out = length(colors)),
			colors
		),
		"</linearGradient>"
	)
}
```

## Building the sticker

### The word

The word, 1000 units to the em, on a level baseline, starting at 0. It is
scaled and placed once there is a swoosh to fit it to.

```{r}
letters <- outlines(word)
letters$x <- letters$x - min(letters$x)
```

### The swoosh

Shiny's wordmark is one path in its sticker, and the fourth subpath of that is
"hiny" joined to the swoosh. Nine of its segments are the swoosh. Segment 168
is its lower edge, from its head as far as under the "n", and segment 1 the
rest of that edge, to the tip of the fin. Segment 4 is the far edge of the fin,
from its tip to the tip of the tail. Segments 7 and 8 are the upper edge, back
to the head. The segments between round the two tips. The stroke that joins the
head to the "y" is left out.

Below, the nine are numbered in that order: 1 and 2 are the lower edge, 5 the
far edge of the fin, and 8 and 9 the upper edge.

```{r}
swoosh <- leveled(parse_path(shiny_path("st2"))[[4]])[c(168, 1:8), ]

# Points on the swoosh, where they are on the sticker before the swoosh and
# the funnel are moved to their place
swoosh_on_sticker <- function(points) {
	points <- sweep(sweep(points, 2, swoosh_cut), 2, swoosh_stretch, "*")
	sweep(
		turned(points, swoosh_tilt - climb) * swoosh_scale,
		2,
		swoosh_at,
		"+"
	)
}

# The handles of those nine segments, on the sticker
swoosh <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(swoosh)), function(i) {
	swoosh_on_sticker(handles(swoosh[i, ]))
})

# The far edge of the fin is all but an arc of a circle: this one, which it
# is nowhere more than 4 units off
fin_circle <- circle_through(bezier(swoosh[[5]], seq(0, 1, length.out = 200)))
```

### The head

The lower edge of the head stops where Shiny's does, curving along a circle. It
runs on round that circle for `swoosh_run` degrees, to the tip. The upper edge
is carried on to the tip too, and comes into it along the circle, so that the
head ends in a point that lies on the circle and along it.

`head_spoke` runs from the middle of the circle to where the lower edge stops,
`head_way` is the way the edge is running as it gets there, and `head_turn` is
which way round the circle that is: 1 for clockwise.

```{r}
head_circle <- circle_at_start(swoosh[[1]])
head_spoke <- swoosh[[1]][1, ] - head_circle$middle
head_way <- unit(swoosh[[1]][1, ] - swoosh[[1]][2, ])
head_turn <- sign(head_spoke[1] * head_way[2] - head_spoke[2] * head_way[1])

# The point this many degrees round the head's circle from where the lower
# edge stops, and the way the circle is running there
round_head <- function(degrees) {
	angle <- atan2(head_spoke[2], head_spoke[1]) + head_turn * degrees * pi / 180
	list(
		at = head_circle$middle + head_circle$radius * c(cos(angle), sin(angle)),
		way = head_turn * c(-sin(angle), cos(angle))
	)
}

# The curve that carries the upper edge on to the tip. It leaves the upper
# edge the way that edge is running, and comes into the tip the way the circle
# is, with handles a third as long as it is from one end to the other.
head_tip <- round_head(swoosh_run)
head_edge <- swoosh[[9]]
head_reach <- sqrt(sum((head_tip$at - head_edge[4, ])^2)) / 3
head_close <- rbind(
	head_edge[4, ],
	head_edge[4, ] + head_reach * unit(head_edge[4, ] - head_edge[3, ]),
	head_tip$at - head_reach * head_tip$way,
	head_tip$at
)

# The lower edge of the swoosh, and how far down it is at x
lower_edge <- swoosh[1:2]
under_swoosh <- function(x) {
	for (curve in lower_edge) {
		if (x >= min(curve[c(1, 4), 1]) && x <= max(curve[c(1, 4), 1])) {
			t <- uniroot(
				function(t) bezier(curve, t)[1] - x,
				c(0, 1),
				tol = 1e-12
			)$root
			return(bezier(curve, t)[2])
		}
	}
}

# Points round the swoosh, from the tip of its head and back to it
swoosh <- rbind(
	t(vapply(
		seq(swoosh_run, 0, length.out = 60)[-60],
		function(degrees) round_head(degrees)$at,
		c(0, 0)
	)),
	do.call(rbind, lapply(swoosh, bezier)),
	bezier(head_close)
)
```

### The funnel

The funnel is drawn with a thick line of its own color round it, which rounds
its corners. Where a side of the cone turns down into the spout, the edge of
the funnel has a corner. It is `reach` out from the corner of the shape that
the line is drawn round and, for a side at `angle` to the spout,
`reach * tan(angle / 2)` below it.

```{r}
reach <- funnel_round / 2
```

The top of the funnel is as wide as the circle of the fin. And it is where the
circle of the head is at its highest: that point is where the top edge of the
funnel stops and the round of its right corner starts. The corner is a smaller
circle that touches the head's there from inside, so the head, carried on, runs
into the top of the funnel without a turn.

These are of the shape that the funnel's line is drawn round: half the width of
its mouth, and where the middle and the top of its mouth are.

```{r}
funnel_mouth <- fin_circle$radius - reach
funnel_x <- head_circle$middle[1] - funnel_mouth
funnel_top <- head_circle$middle[2] - head_circle$radius + reach
```

The funnel is widest down its lip, where its sides run straight down from its
top. Put the circle of the fin on the funnel, with its middle half way down the
lip, and it is as wide as the funnel. The lip is as high as it takes for that
circle to rest on the lower edge of the swoosh: to touch it, and not cross it.
So no funnel shows between the swoosh and the circle.

`below_circle()` is how far the lower edge is below the lowest that the circle
is at x, for a circle with its middle level with 0. Where that is least is
where they touch, and it is how far down the middle of the circle is.

```{r}
below_circle <- function(x) {
	under_swoosh(x) - sqrt(fin_circle$radius^2 - (x - funnel_x)^2)
}
funnel_rest <- optimize(below_circle, funnel_x + c(-1, 1) * funnel_mouth)
funnel_lip <- 2 * (funnel_rest$objective - funnel_top)
funnel_rest <- c(funnel_rest$minimum, under_swoosh(funnel_rest$minimum))
```

The cone is symmetrical: its sides are at the same angle to the spout. Each
runs down until that corner is on the lower edge of the swoosh, so that the
swoosh covers the neck on both sides. The swoosh climbs, so the right side
stops higher than the left, and a spout of a set width hangs right of the
middle of the mouth. This finds the angle of the sides and how far right the
spout hangs.

```{r}
# Height of the neck on a side (-1 left, 1 right), for a spout this far right
neck <- function(side, angle, right) {
	run <- funnel_mouth - funnel_spout - side * right
	funnel_top + funnel_lip + run / tan(angle)
}

# The angle that puts the corner on that side on the swoosh
fitted <- function(side, right) {
	x <- funnel_x + right + side * (funnel_spout + reach)
	uniroot(
		function(angle) {
			neck(side, angle, right) + reach * tan(angle / 2) - under_swoosh(x)
		},
		c(0.2, 1.2),
		tol = 1e-12
	)$root
}

funnel_right <- uniroot(
	function(right) fitted(-1, right) - fitted(1, right),
	c(-100, 100),
	tol = 1e-10
)$root
funnel_angle <- fitted(1, funnel_right)
funnel_neck <- c(
	neck(-1, funnel_angle, funnel_right),
	neck(1, funnel_angle, funnel_right)
)
```

### Where things sit

The swoosh and the funnel go at the top of the sticker, and the word at the
bottom, as on most hex stickers. Each is as far that way as it can be with
`margin` between it and the border.

```{r}
# How far points reach towards the side of the sticker at an hour of the
# clock, from its middle, and how far that side is
reach_to <- function(points, hour) {
	max(sweep(points, 2, size / 2) %*% c(on_clock(hour, 1, c(0, 0))))
}
side_at <- size[1] / 2 - edge_width
```

The swoosh and the funnel are moved, together, so that the swoosh is in the
middle from side to side, and then up, until the first of them is `margin` from
one of the two upper sides. Of the funnel, it is the round of a top corner that
is nearest.

```{r}
funnel_corners <- cbind(funnel_x + c(-1, 1) * funnel_mouth, funnel_top)
emblem_move <- c(size[1] / 2 - mean(range(swoosh[, 1])), 0)
emblem_move[2] <- max(vapply(
	c(11, 1),
	function(hour) {
		towards <- c(on_clock(hour, 1, c(0, 0)))
		reached <- max(
			reach_to(swoosh, hour),
			reach_to(funnel_corners, hour) + reach
		)
		(side_at - margin - reached - emblem_move[1] * towards[1]) / towards[2]
	},
	0
))
```

The word is as wide as the swoosh, so each starts and ends where the other
does. It is in the middle from side to side, and as far down as it can be with
`margin` between it and the two lower sides.

```{r}
word_width <- diff(range(swoosh[, 1]))
word_scale <- word_width / max(letters$x)
letters$x <- (size[1] - word_width) / 2 + letters$x * word_scale
letters$y <- letters$y * word_scale
word_base <- min(vapply(
	c(5, 7),
	function(hour) {
		towards <- c(on_clock(hour, 1, c(0, 0)))
		reached <- reach_to(as.matrix(letters[c("x", "y")]), hour)
		(side_at - margin - reached) / towards[2]
	},
	0
))
letters$y <- letters$y + word_base
```

The spout stops `margin` above the word, where it is longest. `funnel_end` is
where it ends before the swoosh and the funnel are moved: left, right.

```{r}
funnel_end <- min(letters$y) -
	margin -
	reach -
	emblem_move[2] -
	c(funnel_cut, 0)
letters <- lapply(split(letters[c("x", "y")], letters$contour), as.matrix)

# The corners of the shape that the funnel's line is drawn round
funnel_at <- cbind(
	funnel_x +
		c(-1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, -1) * funnel_mouth +
		c(0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0) * funnel_right +
		c(0, 0, 0, 1, 1, -1, -1, 0) * funnel_spout,
	c(
		funnel_top,
		funnel_top,
		funnel_top + funnel_lip,
		funnel_neck[2],
		funnel_end[2],
		funnel_end[1],
		funnel_neck[1],
		funnel_top + funnel_lip
	)
)
```

### The shapes

The shapes are each written once, with no color, and drawn as often as they are
needed, in the colors they are needed in.

```{r}
shapes <- c(
	sprintf(
		'<path id="shape-letters" d="%s"/>',
		path_data(letters)
	),
	sprintf('<path id="shape-swoosh" d="%s"/>', path_data(list(swoosh))),
	sprintf(
		'<polygon id="shape-funnel" stroke-linejoin="round" points="%s"/>',
		points(funnel_at[, 1], funnel_at[, 2])
	)
)

# A shape in a color, with a line this wide round it in the same color
drawn <- function(shape, color, width = 0) {
	sprintf(
		'<use xlink:href="#shape-%s" fill="%s" stroke="%s" stroke-width="%s"/>',
		shape,
		color,
		color,
		width
	)
}

# What moves the swoosh and the funnel to where they go
emblem <- sprintf(
	'<g transform="translate(%.1f,%.1f)">',
	emblem_move[1],
	emblem_move[2]
)
```

### The colors of the funnel

```{r}
# The red, green and blue of a color, each from 0 to 255
parts <- function(color) {
	strtoi(substring(color, c(2, 4, 6), c(3, 5, 7)), 16)
}

# How bright a color is, from 0 for black to 1 for white: what WCAG calls
# its relative luminance. One color stands out from a darker one by
# `(brightness + 0.05) / (the darker one's brightness + 0.05)`, which WCAG
# calls their contrast ratio.
brightness <- function(color) {
	part <- parts(color) / 255
	part <- ifelse(part <= 0.03928, part / 12.92, ((part + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4)
	sum(part * c(0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722))
}

# The color of the sticker this far down it: it fades evenly from the first
# of its colors at the top of the sticker to the second at the bottom
sky_at <- function(y) {
	ends <- vapply(sky, parts, c(0, 0, 0))
	mixed <- round(ends[, 1] + (ends[, 2] - ends[, 1]) * y / size[2])
	sprintf("#%02X%02X%02X", mixed[1], mixed[2], mixed[3])
}

# The magenta that stands out from a darker color by `contrast`. It is the
# magenta that heads a printed <shinyfilters> object, #BB00BB, made lighter
# or darker: as much red as blue, and no green. Its red and blue are rounded
# up, so that it stands out by no less.
magenta_on <- function(color) {
	part <- (contrast * (brightness(color) + 0.05) - 0.05) / (0.2126 + 0.0722)
	part <- ceiling(255 * (1.055 * part^(1 / 2.4) - 0.055))
	sprintf("#%02X00%02X", part, part)
}
```

The funnel fades as the sticker does behind it, from its top to the end of its
spout, and stands out from the sticker by `contrast` at both. Between them it
stands out by nearly as much: with these colors, by 3.11 to 3.13.

```{r}
funnel_span <- c(funnel_top - reach, funnel_end[2] + reach)
funnel_fill <- vapply(
	funnel_span + emblem_move[2],
	function(y) magenta_on(sky_at(y)),
	""
)
```

### The picture

```{r}
svg <- c(
	sprintf(
		paste0(
			'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"',
			' xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" viewBox="0 0 %s %s">'
		),
		size[1],
		size[2]
	),
	"<title>shinyfilters</title>",
	"<defs>",
	gradient("sky", sky, c(0, 0), c(0, size[2])),
	gradient("funnel", funnel_fill, c(0, funnel_span[1]), c(0, funnel_span[2])),
	shapes,
	"</defs>",
	sprintf('<polygon fill="%s" points="%s"/>', edge, hexagon(0)),
	sprintf('<polygon fill="url(#sky)" points="%s"/>', hexagon(edge_width)),
	emblem,
	drawn("funnel", "url(#funnel)", funnel_round),
	drawn("swoosh", ink),
	"</g>",
	drawn("letters", ink),
	"</svg>"
)
```

Each picture in this article is written as an SVG among the article's figures,
and shown.

```{r logo, fig.alt = "The shinyfilters logo: a dark purple hex sticker with a magenta funnel at the top, a white swoosh across the funnel, and the word shinyfilters in white across the bottom."}
# Writes a picture among the article's figures, and shows it. Run by hand, it
# writes a temporary file instead.
draw <- function(svg, name) {
  knitting <- isTRUE(getOption("knitr.in.progress"))
  to <- if (knitting) knitr::opts_chunk$get("fig.path") else tempfile()
  file <- paste0(to, name, ".svg")
  dir.create(dirname(file), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  writeLines(svg, file)
  
  # Wrap in container with forced light-mode filter overrides
  res <- knitr::include_graphics(file)
  attr(res, "class") <- "no-dark-mode"
  res
}

draw(svg, "logo")
```

## Diagrams

The rest of this article draws over the logo, to show that each thing said of
it above is so. These are diagrams, not logos.

### Marks

```{r}
marks <- c("#00E5FF", "#FFB000") # two colors, to tell two things apart
mark_width <- 8
mark_dashes <- c(26, 16)
```

Where a picture rings a place to draw it again, enlarged, the ring is this
size, and what is in it is drawn this many times as large. The enlarged places
have these middles: in [the neck](#neck), the left corner and the right, and in
[the fin](#fin), where the circle rests.

```{r}
ring <- 57.5
zoom <- 4
loupe <- rbind(c(500, 1050), c(2060, 1560))
fin_loupe <- c(2060, 1560)
```

In [the contrast](#contrast), `sampled` is how far down the funnel each ringed
place is: 0 is its top and 1 the end of its spout. They miss the swoosh. And
`figure_height` is how tall the figures are.

```{r}
sampled <- c(0.06, 0.17, 0.32, 0.68, 0.8)
figure_height <- 62
```

### Drawing over the logo

```{r}
# The swoosh and the funnel are worked out in one place and then moved to
# another. This moves points with them.
moved <- function(points) {
	sweep(matrix(points, ncol = 2), 2, emblem_move, "+")
}

# An element drawn as a line in a color, over a wider black one, so that it
# shows on anything
mark <- function(element, color, width = mark_width, dashed = FALSE) {
	dashes <- if (dashed) {
		sprintf(' stroke-dasharray="%s"', paste(mark_dashes, collapse = " "))
	} else {
		""
	}
	sprintf(
		'<%s fill="none" stroke="%s" stroke-width="%s"%s/>',
		element,
		c("#000000", color),
		width + c(6, 0),
		dashes
	)
}

circle <- function(middle, radius) {
	sprintf('circle cx="%.1f" cy="%.1f" r="%.1f"', middle[1], middle[2], radius)
}

# A line through points, one in each row
line <- function(through) {
	through <- sprintf("%.1f,%.1f", through[, 1], through[, 2])
	sprintf('path d="M%s"', paste(through, collapse = "L"))
}

dot <- function(middle, color, radius = 12) {
	sprintf(
		'<%s fill="%s" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="%s"/>',
		circle(middle, radius),
		color,
		radius / 2
	)
}

# What keeps a drawing to the circle that a place is enlarged in
lens <- function(id, to) {
	sprintf(
		'<clipPath id="lens-%s"><%s/></clipPath>',
		id,
		circle(to, ring * zoom)
	)
}

# Where a point of the picture is when the place `from` is enlarged at `to`
enlarged_at <- function(point, from, to) {
	to + zoom * (point - from)
}

# The place `from` again, enlarged, in a circle at `to` that is joined to the
# ring round `from`. `within` is drawn in that circle too, over the picture.
magnified <- function(from, to, id, color, within = NULL) {
	towards <- unit(to - from)
	c(
		sprintf('<g clip-path="url(#lens-%s)">', id),
		sprintf(
			paste0(
				'<use xlink:href="#picture"',
				' transform="translate(%.1f,%.1f) scale(%s) translate(%.1f,%.1f)"/>'
			),
			to[1],
			to[2],
			zoom,
			-from[1],
			-from[2]
		),
		within,
		"</g>",
		mark(circle(to, ring * zoom), color),
		mark(circle(from, ring), color),
		mark(
			line(rbind(from + ring * towards, to - ring * zoom * towards)),
			color
		)
	)
}

# The logo with more drawn on it. `under` is part of the picture, and is
# enlarged with it in `neck`. `over` is not, and none of it shows past the
# edge of the sticker.
diagram <- function(over, under = NULL, defs = NULL) {
	drawn_from <- match("</defs>", svg)
	c(
		svg[seq_len(drawn_from - 1)],
		sprintf(
			'<clipPath id="sticker"><polygon points="%s"/></clipPath>',
			hexagon(0)
		),
		defs,
		"</defs>",
		'<g id="picture">',
		svg[(drawn_from + 1):(length(svg) - 1)],
		under,
		"</g>",
		'<g clip-path="url(#sticker)">',
		over,
		"</g>",
		"</svg>"
	)
}
```

### Fin

The top of the funnel is as wide as the circle that the far edge of the
swoosh's fin lies on, and that circle, with its middle half way down the
funnel's lip, rests on the lower edge of the swoosh. The circle is drawn on the
fin, and again on the funnel, with a line across it. Where it rests on the
swoosh is ringed, and drawn again, enlarged, in a circle.

```{r fin, fig.alt = "The logo with the circle of the swoosh's fin drawn on the fin and again on the funnel, where it is as wide as the funnel's top. The place where it rests on the swoosh is enlarged."}
# The fin's circle where it is, with a line from its middle to its edge. And
# again with its middle on the funnel, half way down its lip, with the same
# line each way: it ends on the edge of the funnel on each side.
across <- rbind(c(-1, 0), c(1, 0)) * fin_circle$radius
on_fin <- c(moved(fin_circle$middle))
on_funnel <- c(moved(c(funnel_x, funnel_top + funnel_lip / 2)))

# Where the circle on the funnel rests on the lower edge of the swoosh. It is
# drawn again, enlarged, with the circle drawn over it at the same weight of
# line: the swoosh is on one side of the circle there and the funnel on the
# other, with none of the funnel between the swoosh and the circle.
rests <- c(moved(funnel_rest))

draw(
	diagram(
		defs = lens("rest", fin_loupe),
		over = c(
			mark(circle(on_funnel, fin_circle$radius), marks[2], 4),
			mark(line(sweep(across, 2, on_funnel, "+")), marks[2]),
			dot(on_funnel, marks[2]),
			dot(on_funnel + across[1, ], marks[2]),
			dot(on_funnel + across[2, ], marks[2]),
			mark(circle(on_fin, fin_circle$radius), marks[1]),
			mark(line(rbind(on_fin, on_fin + across[2, ])), marks[1]),
			dot(on_fin, marks[1]),
			dot(on_fin + across[2, ], marks[1]),
			magnified(
				rests,
				fin_loupe,
				"rest",
				marks[2],
				within = mark(
					circle(
						enlarged_at(on_funnel, rests, fin_loupe),
						zoom * fin_circle$radius
					),
					marks[2],
					4
				)
			)
		)
	),
	"fin"
)
```

### Head

The head of the swoosh runs on round the circle that its lower edge is curving
along, and that circle, carried on, is at its highest where the top edge of the
funnel stops and its corner starts. The circle, the run of the head, the rest
of the way to the funnel, the line of the funnel's top and the circle of its
corner are drawn.

```{r head, fig.alt = "The logo with the circle of the swoosh's head drawn. The head runs part of the way round it, and it is at its highest on the line of the funnel's top, where the funnel's right corner starts."}
# How far round its circle the head would have to run to be at its highest
head_top <- (head_turn *
	(-90 - atan2(head_spoke[2], head_spoke[1]) * 180 / pi)) %%
	360

# The points on the head's circle from this many degrees round to that
head_arc <- function(from, to) {
	arc <- vapply(
		seq(from, to, length.out = 200),
		function(degrees) round_head(degrees)$at,
		c(0, 0)
	)
	moved(t(arc))
}

# The line of the top edge of the funnel, carried on each way past where the
# circle touches it. And the round of the funnel's right corner, as a whole
# circle: the head's circle touches it, and the top edge, at the same point.
highest <- c(moved(round_head(head_top)$at))
level_with <- sweep(rbind(c(-300, 0), c(300, 0)), 2, highest, "+")
corner_circle <- circle(moved(c(funnel_x + funnel_mouth, funnel_top)), reach)

draw(
	diagram(c(
		mark(line(level_with), marks[2], 4, dashed = TRUE),
		mark(corner_circle, marks[2], 4),
		mark(
			circle(moved(head_circle$middle), head_circle$radius),
			marks[1],
			4,
			dashed = TRUE
		),
		mark(line(head_arc(0, swoosh_run)), marks[2]),
		mark(line(head_arc(swoosh_run, head_top)), marks[1]),
		mark(circle(highest, 30), marks[1]),
		dot(moved(round_head(0)$at), marks[2]),
		dot(moved(head_tip$at), marks[1])
	)),
	"head"
)
```

### Neck

The cone ends on the lower edge of the swoosh on both sides, and is
symmetrical. Each corner where the cone turns down into the spout is ringed,
and drawn again, enlarged, in a circle. The edges of the cone are carried on
under the swoosh to those corners, and on down to where they meet, which is
under the middle of the mouth.

```{r neck, fig.alt = "The logo with the two corners where the funnel's cone turns into its spout enlarged: each lies on the lower edge of the swoosh. The edges of the cone are carried on to meet under the middle of the funnel's mouth."}
# On a side (-1 left, 1 right): the way out of the cone through that side,
# and the way down along it
out_of <- function(side) {
	c(side * cos(funnel_angle), sin(funnel_angle))
}
down <- function(side) {
	c(-side * sin(funnel_angle), cos(funnel_angle))
}

# The corner in the edge of the funnel where the cone turns down into the
# spout
corner <- function(side) {
	moved(c(
		funnel_x + funnel_right + side * (funnel_spout + reach),
		funnel_neck[(side + 3) / 2] + reach * tan(funnel_angle / 2)
	))
}

# Where the edge of that side of the cone starts, under the lip. And where
# the two edges would meet if they were carried on down: it is under the
# middle of the mouth, because the sides are at the same angle.
edge_from <- function(side) {
	lip <- c(funnel_x + side * funnel_mouth, funnel_top + funnel_lip)
	moved(lip + reach * out_of(side))
}
apex <- edge_from(1) +
	down(1) * (edge_from(1)[1] - moved(c(funnel_x, 0))[1]) / sin(funnel_angle)

draw(
	diagram(
		defs = c(
			'<clipPath id="under-swoosh">',
			sprintf('<path d="%s"/>', path_data(list(moved(swoosh)))),
			"</clipPath>",
			lens("left", loupe[1, ]),
			lens("right", loupe[2, ])
		),
		under = c(
			# The edges of the cone where the swoosh hides them
			'<g clip-path="url(#under-swoosh)">',
			mark(line(rbind(edge_from(-1), corner(-1))), marks[1], dashed = TRUE),
			mark(line(rbind(edge_from(1), corner(1))), marks[2], dashed = TRUE),
			"</g>",
			dot(corner(-1), marks[1], 5),
			dot(corner(1), marks[2], 5)
		),
		over = c(
			# The edges carried on to where they meet, and the middle of the mouth
			mark(line(rbind(corner(-1), apex)), marks[1], 4, dashed = TRUE),
			mark(line(rbind(corner(1), apex)), marks[2], 4, dashed = TRUE),
			mark(
				line(rbind(moved(c(funnel_x, funnel_top - reach)), apex)),
				"#FFFFFF",
				4,
				dashed = TRUE
			),
			dot(apex, "#FFFFFF"),
			magnified(c(corner(-1)), loupe[1, ], "left", marks[1]),
			magnified(c(corner(1)), loupe[2, ], "right", marks[2])
		)
	),
	"neck"
)
```

### Place

The swoosh is in the middle of the sticker and the word is as wide as it, and
the same margin, as wide as the border, is left at the top, at the bottom, and
between the spout and the word. The middle and the ends are drawn as lines, and
each margin as a circle that just fits it. One more of those circles is drawn
on the border.

```{r place, fig.alt = "The logo with lines down the middle of the sticker and down from each end of the swoosh to each end of the word, and small circles of one size that just fit the margins at the top, at the bottom, and between the spout and the word."}
# The way to the side of the sticker at an hour of the clock, and the point
# among some that is furthest that way
towards <- function(hour) {
	c(on_clock(hour, 1, c(0, 0)))
}
furthest <- function(points, hour) {
	points[which.max(points %*% towards(hour)), ]
}

# A circle as wide as the margin, touching a point, on the side of it that
# is this way. If the margin is right, it just fits.
gauge <- function(point, way, color = marks[2]) {
	c(
		mark(circle(point + margin / 2 * way, margin / 2), color, 4),
		dot(point, color, 6)
	)
}

swoosh_now <- moved(swoosh)
letters_now <- do.call(rbind, letters)
ends <- range(swoosh_now[, 1])
word_top <- min(letters_now[, 2])

# The nearest of the swoosh to the border at the top, of the word to it at
# the bottom, and of the spout to the word
nearest_top <- furthest(swoosh_now, 1)
nearest_bottom <- furthest(letters_now, 7)
spout_end <- c(moved(funnel_at[5, ])) + c(0, reach)

draw(
	diagram(c(
		# The middle of the sticker, and of the swoosh
		mark(
			line(cbind(size[1] / 2, c(edge_width, size[2] - edge_width))),
			"#FFFFFF",
			4,
			dashed = TRUE
		),
		mark(line(cbind(ends, mean(swoosh_now[, 2]))), marks[1], 4),
		dot(c(mean(ends), mean(swoosh_now[, 2])), marks[1]),
		# The ends of the swoosh, carried down to the ends of the word
		mark(
			line(cbind(ends[1], c(min(swoosh_now[, 2]), max(letters_now[, 2])))),
			marks[1],
			4,
			dashed = TRUE
		),
		mark(
			line(cbind(ends[2], c(min(swoosh_now[, 2]), max(letters_now[, 2])))),
			marks[1],
			4,
			dashed = TRUE
		),
		# The top of the word, which the spout stops short of
		mark(line(cbind(ends, word_top)), marks[2], 4, dashed = TRUE),
		# The margins, and the border, which is as wide
		gauge(nearest_top, towards(1)),
		gauge(nearest_top + margin * towards(1), towards(1), "#FFFFFF"),
		gauge(nearest_bottom, towards(7)),
		gauge(nearest_bottom + margin * towards(7), towards(7), "#FFFFFF"),
		gauge(spout_end, c(0, 1))
	)),
	"place"
)
```

### Contrast

The funnel stands out from the sticker by the same amount all the way down, and
the white of the swoosh stands out from the funnel by more. Five places on the
edge of the funnel are ringed in one color, each with how much the funnel
stands out from the sticker there, as WCAG measures contrast. Two places where
the swoosh crosses the funnel are ringed in the other, each with how much the
white stands out from the funnel there.

```{r contrast, fig.alt = "The logo with five places ringed down the left edge of the funnel, each marked with a contrast ratio a little over 3, and two places ringed where the swoosh crosses the funnel, each marked with a ratio near 4.9."}
# A color part of the way from one to another, as red, green and blue
between <- function(colors, share) {
	ends <- vapply(colors, parts, c(0, 0, 0))
	ends[, 1] + (ends[, 2] - ends[, 1]) * share
}

# How bright red, green and blue are together, as `brightness()` has it
bright <- function(part) {
	part <- part / 255
	part <- ifelse(part <= 0.03928, part / 12.92, ((part + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4)
	sum(part * c(0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722))
}

# The left edge of the funnel, this far down it before it is moved: on the
# lip, on the cone, or on the spout
left_edge <- function(y) {
	lip <- funnel_top + funnel_lip
	start <- c(funnel_x - funnel_mouth, lip) + reach * out_of(-1)
	turn <- funnel_neck[1] + reach * tan(funnel_angle / 2)
	if (y <= start[2]) {
		funnel_x - funnel_mouth - reach
	} else if (y <= turn) {
		start[1] + (y - start[2]) * tan(funnel_angle)
	} else {
		funnel_x + funnel_right - funnel_spout - reach
	}
}

# Figures, as shapes, this tall, ending at a point, or starting at it if
# `after`
figures <- function(text, at, after = FALSE) {
	shapes <- outlines(text)
	scale <- figure_height / diff(range(outlines("0")$y))
	from <- if (after) min(shapes$x) else max(shapes$x)
	shapes$x <- at[1] + (shapes$x - from) * scale
	shapes$y <- at[2] + shapes$y * scale + figure_height / 2
	shapes <- path_data(lapply(
		split(shapes[c("x", "y")], shapes$contour),
		as.matrix
	))
	c(
		sprintf(
			paste0(
				'<path fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="14"',
				' stroke-linejoin="round" d="%s"/>'
			),
			shapes
		),
		sprintf('<path fill="#FFFFFF" d="%s"/>', shapes)
	)
}

# A place on the edge of the funnel, ringed, with how much the funnel stands
# out from the sticker there
stands_out <- function(share) {
	y <- funnel_span[1] + share * diff(funnel_span)
	at <- c(moved(c(left_edge(y), y)))
	funnel <- bright(between(funnel_fill, share))
	sticker <- bright(between(sky, at[2] / size[2]))
	c(
		mark(circle(at, 40), marks[1], 5),
		figures(
			sprintf("%.2f", (funnel + 0.05) / (sticker + 0.05)),
			at - c(64, 0)
		)
	)
}

# How far down the upper and the lower edge of the swoosh are at x, before
# it is moved
swoosh_edges <- function(x) {
	to <- swoosh[c(2:nrow(swoosh), 1), ]
	crosses <- (swoosh[, 1] - x) * (to[, 1] - x) < 0
	share <- (x - swoosh[crosses, 1]) / (to[crosses, 1] - swoosh[crosses, 1])
	range(swoosh[crosses, 2] + share * (to[crosses, 2] - swoosh[crosses, 2]))
}

# A place where an edge of the swoosh crosses the funnel, before it is moved,
# ringed, with how much the white of the swoosh stands out from the funnel
# there. The figures go on the funnel: up and to the left of a place on the
# upper edge, and down and to the right of one on the lower.
white_on <- function(at, upper) {
	funnel <- bright(between(
		funnel_fill,
		(at[2] - funnel_span[1]) / diff(funnel_span)
	))
	at <- c(moved(at))
	c(
		mark(circle(at, 40), marks[2], 5),
		figures(
			sprintf("%.2f", (bright(parts(ink)) + 0.05) / (funnel + 0.05)),
			at + if (upper) c(-64, -50) else c(64, 50),
			after = !upper
		)
	)
}

# The upper edge of the swoosh where it is over the right of the spout, and
# its lower edge where it is over the left of the spout
on_upper <- funnel_x + funnel_right + 0.6 * funnel_spout
on_upper <- c(on_upper, swoosh_edges(on_upper)[1])
on_lower <- funnel_x + funnel_right - 0.6 * funnel_spout
on_lower <- c(on_lower, swoosh_edges(on_lower)[2])

draw(
	diagram(c(
		unlist(lapply(sampled, stands_out)),
		white_on(on_upper, upper = TRUE),
		white_on(on_lower, upper = FALSE)
	)),
	"contrast"
)
```

## Files

Of all this, the package keeps one file: the logo, as `man/figures/logo.svg`.
To write it again, run the chunks above from the top of the package, and then:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
writeLines(svg, "man/figures/logo.svg")
```

The site's favicons are the logo too, in the middle of a square with nothing
round it. They are kept in `pkgdown/favicon`, which is not part of the built
package, and are made with magick:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(magick)

favicons <- "pkgdown/favicon"
master_height <- 512

# Rasterized at twice the size, to be scaled down for clean edges
rasterize <- function(svg) {
	file <- tempfile(fileext = ".svg")
	writeLines(svg, file)
	image_read(file, density = 96 * 2 * master_height / size[2])
}

# magick paints SVG onto white. To keep the corners transparent, paint the
# canvas in the border color, then cut the hexagon out with its silhouette.
canvas <- sprintf('<rect width="%s" height="%s" fill="%%s"/>', size[1], size[2])
master <- rasterize(append(svg, sprintf(canvas, edge), after = 1))
silhouette <- rasterize(c(
	svg[1],
	sprintf(canvas, "#000"),
	sprintf('<polygon fill="#fff" points="%s"/>', hexagon(0)),
	"</svg>"
))
silhouette <- image_convert(silhouette, type = "Grayscale", matte = FALSE)
master <- image_composite(master, silhouette, operator = "CopyOpacity")

# The logo this many pixels high, in the middle of a square
icon <- function(pixels) {
	logo <- image_resize(master, paste0("x", pixels))
	image_extent(logo, paste0(pixels, "x", pixels), color = "none")
}

# An icon written among the favicons, as a PNG
png <- function(pixels, name) {
	image_write(icon(pixels), file.path(favicons, name), format = "png")
}

dir.create(favicons, showWarnings = FALSE)
writeLines(svg, file.path(favicons, "favicon.svg"))
png(96, "favicon-96x96.png")
png(180, "apple-touch-icon.png")
png(192, "web-app-manifest-192x192.png")
png(512, "web-app-manifest-512x512.png")

# One file with the icon at each of these sizes, for whatever size it is shown
# at: at the largest only, it is blurred when shown larger
image_write(
	image_join(lapply(c(16, 32, 48, 64, 128, 256), icon)),
	file.path(favicons, "favicon.ico"),
	format = "ico"
)

# The icons that the site offers a phone to keep it by
manifest_icon <- '{"src": "web-app-manifest-%1$sx%1$s.png", "sizes": "%1$sx%1$s", "type": "image/png"}'
writeLines(
	c(
		"{",
		'  "name": "shinyfilters",',
		'  "short_name": "shinyfilters",',
		'  "icons": [',
		sprintf(paste0("    ", manifest_icon, "%2$s"), c(192, 512), c(",", "")),
		"  ],",
		sprintf('  "theme_color": "%s",', sky[1]),
		sprintf('  "background_color": "%s",', sky[2]),
		'  "display": "standalone"',
		"}"
	),
	file.path(favicons, "site.webmanifest")
)
```
